title: Getting started for private developers
snippet: Before creating a private application, you must first be registered as an Amazon Seller using [Amazon Seller Central](https://sellercentral.amazon.com/?ld=NSGoogle&pageName=US%3ASPDS%3ASPAPI-private-developer). Only Professional Selling Accounts can register to develop or integrate with Selling Partner API. Individual accounts are not eligible. You can upgrade your account to a professional plan at any time.

title: Selling Partner API Roles
snippet:
Roles are the mechanism by which the Selling Partner API (SP-API) determines whether a developer or application has access to an operation or resource. Roles protect access to personally identifiable information (PII) and other sensitive data, and ensure that developers only access data that their application requires.
As a developer, you must request and qualify for a particular role to gain access to the operations and resources that the role provides. If you call an operation for which you don't have the required roles, you get a 403 error.
##
Choose your roles
Use the following topics to identify which role you need for each SP-API operation and type:
- [Role Mappings for Operations](https://developer-docs.amazon.com/sp-api/docs/role-mappings)
- [Role Mappings for Types](https://developer-docs.amazon.com/sp-api/docs/role-mappings-for-types)
After you know which roles you need, you request them through your developer profile. Amazon evaluates the information you submit and approves or denies your request. If denied, you can address the reason for the denial and then resubmit your profile.
###
Add your approved roles to your application
When you [register your SP-API application](https://developer-docs.amazon.com/sp-api/docs/registering-your-application), you can choose roles from among those that you were approved for in your developer profile. If the role that you need is missing, you must update the roles in your developer profile to include the new role, and then resubmit your profile for evaluation by Amazon. If you are approved, the added role will be available to select for your application.

To add a new role:
1. Go to your developer profile and submit the role that you want to add.
2. After your [developer profile is approved](https://developer-docs.amazon.com/sp-api/docs/checking-the-status-of-your-request-to-register-as-a-developer), go to your application configuration and [apply the newly approved role](https://developer-docs.amazon.com/sp-api/docs/updating-your-application-information) to your application. Save the changes and re-list the application.
3. After the application is approved, [get new authorizations](https://developer-docs.amazon.com/sp-api/docs/authorizing-selling-partner-api-applications) to generate a new refresh token that grants access to the API operations, reports, feeds, and notifications that the new role provides.

title: Selling Partner API (SP-API) | Sell on Amazon
snippet:
With Selling Partner API (SP-API), you can build automated solutions for your own sales in the Amazon store. Or you can create and list apps for other Amazon sellers in the [Selling Partner Appstore](https://sell.amazon.com/tools/selling-partner-appstore).

[Selling Partner API (SP-API)](https://developer.amazonservices.com/) is a REST-based API that helps Amazon sellers and vendors programmatically access their data for orders, shipments, payments, and much more. You can integrate automated solutions just for your business, or use SP-API to integrate and list apps in the [Selling Partner Appstore](https://sell.amazon.com/tools/selling-partner-appstore) for use by other Amazon sellers.

Yes, only Professional selling accounts can access Developer Central and integrate with SP-API. If you have an Individual selling account, you can [upgrade at any time](https://sellercentral.amazon.com/help/hub/reference/external/G201747610). For more information, visit [our documentation website](https://developer-docs.amazon.com/sp-api/docs/registering-as-a-developer).

*A Professional selling account is $39.99/month + selling fees. [Learn more](https://sell.amazon.com/pricing#selling-plans)

title: SP API General FAQs
snippet:
Do I need a Professional Selling Account to register as a Selling Partner API developer?
Yes, only Professional Selling Accounts can register to develop or integrate with Selling Partner API. Individual accounts are not eligible. You can upgrade your account to a professional plan at any time. You can view your selling plan type and the marketplace information under “Your Services” in Account info at [https://sellercentral.amazon.com//hz/sc/account-information](https://sellercentral.amazon.com//hz/sc/account-information).

title: SP-API Registration Overview
snippet:
You must register as a Selling Partner API (SP-API) developer before you can [register your Selling Partner API application](https://developer-docs.amazon.com/sp-api/docs/registering-your-application).
The procedure for registering as a developer varies slightly depending on the type of application that you plan to create:
- [Private seller applications](https://developer-docs.amazon.com/sp-api/docs/register-as-a-private-developer): Applications for sellers that are available only to your organization, and are self-authorized. Note that in Seller Central, you must have a professional selling account to develop SP-API private seller applications. Individual accounts are not eligible. You can upgrade your account to a professional plan at any time.
- [Private vendor applications](https://developer-docs.amazon.com/sp-api/docs/register-as-a-private-vendor): Vendor applications that are available only to your organization, and are self-authorized.
- [Public seller and vendor applications](https://developer-docs.amazon.com/sp-api/docs/register-as-a-public-developer): Applications that are publicly available and are authorized by sellers or by vendors using OAuth. In accordance with the [Solution Provider Portal Agreement](https://developer-docs.amazon.com/sp-api/docs/policies-and-agreements), public developers must list their app in the Amazon Selling Partner Appstore.

title: Amazon Selling Partner API: what it takes to get access
snippet:
**TL;DR:** The Amazon Selling Partner API is Amazon's developer interface for reading and managing seller and vendor data. Private seller apps need a professional selling account and a developer profile that Amazon reviews, with roles picked from 17 options. Every call then runs inside per-operation rate limits. Commerce Spine already carries Amazon's approval and gives your own agent a read-only API, starting with a free plan on one account.

Amazon separates three kinds of applications. A private seller app serves only your own organization and you authorize it yourself. A private vendor app does the same for a vendor. A public app is authorized by other sellers or vendors through OAuth and must be listed in the Selling Partner Appstore. [amz-registration]
## Who can get access to the Selling Partner API?
A seller with a professional selling account can register, and only the primary account user can complete it. Individual selling accounts are not eligible for private seller applications, though Amazon lets you upgrade to a professional plan at any time. [amz-registration]
Public developers carry extra requirements. Their website must meet Amazon's guidelines for public developers and service providers, and their app has to appear in the Appstore under the Solution Provider Portal Agreement. Both public and private applications also face authorization limits. [amz-registration]
## How do you register as an SP-API developer?
You register by filling in a Developer Profile from Seller Central, under Apps and Services and then Develop Apps. The form asks for contact information, the data you need, the roles that apply to you, your use cases and your security controls. You then accept the Solution Provider Portal Agreement, the Acceptable Use Policy and the Data Protection Policy, and choose Register. [amz-register]
Amazon asks you to keep the profile under 500 words and to write it yourself instead of copying its policies. The team that owns data security should answer the security questions. Amazon then opens a case with next steps. If it asks for more information, you have five days to respond before the case closes and your access stays unchanged. [amz-registration] [amz-register]
